items.Sentence: The treatment system at the Facility consists of a headworks with one mechanical bar screen, a backup manual screen, a backup comminutor, two activated sludge aeration basins, two secondary clarifiers, one ballast pond to equalize flow to the pressure filters, three pressurized multi-media filtration units, one chlorine contact basin, and sulfur dioxide dechlorination.

The influent pump station is equipped with three dry pit submersible pumps with a pumping capacity of 2.5 MGD each.
Complete Mix Activated Sludge: Flow from the headworks is distributed evenly between the two 420,000-gallon aeration basins. Detention times run from 4 to 8 hours, depending on flows.

The treatment system at the Facility consists of ... three pressurized multi-media filtration units, ... The filter’s maximum surface loading rate is 5 gallons per minute per square foot. Backwash rates are 18,000 gallons to 25,000 gallons per backwash.

Chlorination: Two chlorinators supply a gas solution for disinfection with a maximum feed rate of 400 lbs/day. The dose is applied at the beginning of the 134,000-gallon chlorine contact chamber.

De-chlorination: The effluent discharged from the chlorine contact chamber is dosed with a sodium bisulfite solution. The sodium bisulfite neutralizes any remaining chlorine to have a zero-chlorine residual, leaving the Facility.
Digester: The Facility has two aerobic digesters. Digester No. 1 has a capacity of 256,000 gallons, and Digester No. 2 has a capacity of 453,000 gallons. Currently, only Digester No. 2 is online.

Sludge Stabilization Ponds and Drying Beds: Ponds receive digester decant, wasting, and filter backwash flows. The ponds are decanted back to the headworks at a maximum flow of 0.04 MGD. Ponds are dewatered in the spring to an empty pond. The solids are dried in the pond or in conjunction with the drying beds if solid levels are too high.
The drying beds have an underdrain system that flows back to the headworks. Once the sludge has dried in ponds and beds, it is removed and trucked to the landfill.

The Facility’s emergency storage pond is only used in the event of catastrophic mechanical failures where sufficient treatment cannot be achieved prior to discharge or if there is a 100-year flood and the treatment plant is pushed beyond operational capacity and needs additional storage.
